cost: THE SUBJECT LANDS 70 AGAINST 72 AND THE SIZE WAS DERIVED, NOT FITTED TO HIM. CV_K is 0.26 - 0.11 = 0.15, the load weight minus the conversion weight, which is recal_138's own construction ('paid at the LOAD weight instead of the CREATION weight, and the premium is the gap between them'). The JOINT window in which both subjects sit inside their tolerance is 0.12 to 0.25 and the derived value is inside it; at 0.18 Barry reads exactly 72 and Allen 79. A later round that wants Barry ON 72 can move CV_K to 0.18 without touching anything else and without breaking an anchor — that is measured, not guessed.

THE ANCHOR WALL IS REGGIE MILLER '97 (88 +-1, recal_89) AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE. Every CV_K from 0 to 0.27 holds all 195 anchors; 0.28 takes him to 90. He is the same card as Ray Allen '09 with more load (efficiency 95, volume 85, playvol 50) and the lead-scorer fade is the whole reason he only moves one point. Any later round that widens this term's volume fade is spending his pin first.

THE SCOUT'S PROPOSED MECHANISM IS PROVABLY INSUFFICIENT FOR BARRY AND THAT IS ON THE RECORD. The dispatch asked for 'an efficiency x volume interaction'. Brent Barry '02 and the pinned Kyle Korver '15 differ by 2 on efficiency (96/94), 4 on volume (14/10) and 4 on the arc (91/95); Barry needs +6.57 of o_score to enter his band and Korver has 2.06 before he leaves his, so no function of those three bars can separate them. Measured over 15,600 parameterisations of an efficiency x involvement term with no lead-scorer fade: ZERO feasible, and Reggie Miller '97 fails in all 1,041 of the settings that land both subjects. The fade is what makes the term possible, and it is recal_176's own line.

OFF_TOP IS NOT RE-DERIVED. The OFF raw top is 110.27 before and after and the same 16 cards sit above the band anchor of 102.75, because every card above the knee is either a lead creator (playvol >= 85) or a lead scorer (volume >= 93) or a big. recal_90's cost is not paid this round.

THE TERM SITS BEFORE THE FLOORS, SO A FLOOR CAN STILL ABSORB IT. It is placed immediately after recal_112's efficient-interior block and before recal_64/118's off-ball floor, recal_155's glue floor and recal_182's second-chance floor — a floor is a floor and a card whose standard path now clears it simply stops being floored. Neither subject is floored either way (Barry's arc floor reads 60.76 against a standard path of 75.43).

recal_155's GLUE FLOOR STILL CARRIES A SHOT-DIET GATE AND IT IS THE NEXT THING TO LOOK AT. Its `3pt 68 -> 40` factor shuts the file's only possession-work channel to any card who can shoot, and its own named reason for that gate — 'Kyle Korver '15 would take +2 without it' — was defused by recal_169's used-load ramp, which post-dates it: Korver's glue floor now reads 62.06 against a standard path of 61.92, worth +0.14. Removing the gate was MEASURED this round as an alternative route to the subject: 157 cards move, all up, every anchor holds, and Barry lands at 68 — one printed point short of his band (raw 68.33 against the 68.50 he needs), which is why it is not the round. It remains a real seam for a later ruling.
notes: WHAT THE TWO SCOUT ITEMS SHARE, decomposed. o_score reads a scorer with TWO INDEPENDENT FACTS — `volume` at 0.26 (how many possessions ran through him) and `efficiency` at 0.11 (what he did with them) — and reads their PRODUCT only through recal_26's signature, `0.08 x max(volume, 50) x efficiency / 100`, the smallest weight on the sheet, flat below volume 50 by its own floor. Points are load TIMES conversion. Ray Allen '09 (volume 59 x 0.26 = 15.34 against efficiency 92 x 0.11 = 10.12, o_score 78.41) and Jamal Crawford '09 (volume 76 x 0.26 = 19.76 against efficiency 51 x 0.11 = 5.61, o_score 78.26) printed the SAME 73: seventeen volume points are worth 4.42 and forty-one efficiency points are worth 4.51, and the two cancel. It is the Kaman/Smits shape — usage paid regardless of what it produced — read on the perimeter.

WHY NEITHER EXISTING CHANNEL REACHED THEM, checked rather than assumed. recal_112/139's efficient-interior term is gated by `_e3` (3pt 68 -> 40) — 'efficiency earned at the rim and the line is paid here and efficiency earned from the arc is paid there' — and both subjects shoot (3pt 91 and 90), so it is exactly zero for them; Allen also fails its `_ev` gate (volume 45 -> 35) at 59. recal_64/118's off-ball floor is where `_e3` sends them and it provably does not pay the claim: its vector carries NO load term at all and only ever acts as a floor. Barry's reads 60.76 against a standard path of 67.09 and does not bind; Allen is outside its `volume < 55` gate entirely. The gate routes the arc's conversion to a channel that is empty.

WHY THE LOAD IS THE OFFENCE HE HANDLES AND NOT HIS OWN SHOT. Barry '02 uses 15.4% of his team's possessions — his `volume` is 14 and no term reading volume can lift him past Kyle Korver '15, who reads 10. What he has that Korver has not is the other 5.3 assists a night: playvol 63 against 40. So the quantity is recal_121/186's HANDLING LOAD, `0.5 x (volume + playvol)`, the share of an offence a man moves whether he finishes it or passes it: Korver 25.0, Kerr '96 26.0, Barry 38.5, Allen 51.5, Reggie Miller '97 67.5, Billups '06 77.0. The ramp runs over the class's own p10 and median because a quantile of the class the term pays is the only number in the file's vocabulary for 'a real share' (recal_130's PD_MIN_FULL, recal_163's SECOND_FULL, recal_169's GL_U_FULL, recal_176's PD_V_HI).

THE TWO FADES ARE NOT NEW IDEAS, THEY ARE THE DISJOINTNESS THIS FILE ALREADY BUILDS. A lead creator is priced by recal_109's passer band, so this term runs the same band backwards and the two cross over the same 15 points (playvol 70 -> 85) that recal_154/176 gave the hub and the passer. A lead scorer is priced by the load weight at its largest AND by the signature, which above volume 50 is already linear in volume — this term is the correction BELOW that line, so it fades over recal_176's own measured top decile (volume 93 -> 10). Neither constant is chosen here; both are read off the terms they hand over to.

MEASURED, AND THE MOVERS ARE ONE ARCHETYPE. 481 of 10,000 cards move on OFF, EVERY ONE OF THEM UP, mean +1.86, max +9; DEF and every attribute move on ZERO (the term lives entirely inside o_score); OVR follows on 372, mean +1.58, max +6. The top 12 by OFF and the top 12 by OVR are IDENTICAL, name for name and in order. The class reads like what it is — efficient secondary scorers who handle a real share of an offence without being the man it runs through: Chris Mullin '97 (+8), Mike Miller '08 (+8), Reggie Miller '02 (+7), Kenny Smith '94 (+7), Terry Porter '99 (+6), Sidney Moncrief '82 (+6), Jeff Hornacek '95/'97 (+6), Hersey Hawkins '95-'97 (+5/+6), Steve Smith '01 (+5). Only 41 of the movers are 2021-26 cards and the largest is three points (Michael Porter Jr. '21 71 -> 73, Kon Knueppel '26 77 -> 79, Austin Reaves '24 64 -> 66).

THE VARIANTS THAT WERE MEASURED AND REJECTED. (1) An efficiency x volume interaction, the reading the dispatch proposed: 15,600 parameterisations, ZERO feasible, and of the 1,041 that land both subjects every single one breaks Reggie Miller '97 — the proof is that the correction must know about a man's CREATION, not just his shot. (2) Removing recal_155's glue-floor `3pt` gate, which is a real and separate defect: it reaches Barry through his possession work (drb 46, orb 15, playvol 63 against efficiency 96) and lands him at 68, one printed point short, and does nothing at all for Allen (volume 59 is outside the floor's `volume < 55` gate and his floor computes 63.5 against a standard path of 78.41). (3) Dropping the `not is_big` gate: Nene '11 reads 71 against a 65 +-2 pin and Richaun Holmes '21 reads 66 against 62 +-3 — the big side of this claim is recal_112/139's and it is already paid.
